title.en: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change

text.en: Rani notices that she is taller, her voice and moods are changing and she wants more privacy. These changes are a normal part of growing up called adolescence.

Adolescence is the stage from about 10 to 19 years when a child grows into an adult. Both boys and girls grow taller and gain weight. Boys' voices deepen and facial hair appears. Girls begin menstruation. These changes happen at different times for different people and are completely normal.
Hormones are chemicals made by glands that control the changes of the body. The pituitary gland in the brain controls other glands.
Eat a balanced diet with enough iron and calcium, sleep well, exercise and keep the body clean. Bathe daily, wash hair, change clothes and care for teeth. During menstruation, use clean pads or cloth and change them often.
Mood swings, anger and worry are common in adolescence. Talking to parents, teachers or a trusted adult helps. Choose friends wisely and avoid harmful habits such as tobacco.
